source_findings.defect: A correct reference mapping need not increase every Cartesian roundoff contribution. The old wrong rows overestimated some terms and underestimated others. Requiring the newly derived raw bound to exceed every old value can stop a valid correction before the downstream gates.
source_findings.minimal_fix: Keep raw_corrected_roundoff and old_roundoff as separately named evidence. Check raw_corrected finite/nonnegative; use an upward-rounded elementwise maximum of raw_corrected_roundoff and old_roundoff as the operative roundoff. Preserve the existing monotonicity assertion on that operative array. No covariance/window or tolerance changes.

source_findings.defect: A single nextafter after a rounded positive dot product, weighted reduction or accumulation does not generally enclose all intermediate multiplication/addition roundoff. Exact Fraction reference scales and the per-product q enclosure are useful, but they do not make later vec@base, BA einsum and repeated joint additions directed-rounded. This is a defect in the claimed upward construction, not evidence of inaccurate covariance matrices.
source_findings.minimal_fix: Use upward rounding after each elementary nonnegative product and addition for the three-coordinate dot products and scalar chains. For longer BA and BC positive reductions, use either elementwise directed products plus a directed summation, or an explicitly justified gamma_n accumulation allowance with an operation count covering every product/addition and explicit subnormal/underflow handling. Preserve finite/nonnegative checks. Retain the empirical e_sens/global_rigorous_type3_error_enclosure=NOT_ESTABLISHED ceiling; do not claim certification of FINUFFT or continuum error.
